chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the dowry (mahr), what is it? He said: 'It is that which the people have agreed upon.'

key_terms.النَّاسُ: The people (referring to general custom or 'urf)
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of mahr in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the definition of mahr is rooted in 'urf al-nas' (customary practice) rather than a fixed scriptural amount, highlighting the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in marital contracts. This aligns with the principle that mutual consent (taradhin) is the cornerstone of validity, allowing the dowry to adapt to social norms and economic realities. The hadith underscores the practical application of Quranic injunctions on fair treatment and agreement between spouses.
